package_info.package_manager: Custom Windows malware (not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: ValleyRAT is a multi-stage remote access trojan (RAT) that uses in-memory shellcode, registry persistence, AV evasion, privilege escalation, and C2 communication to fully compromise Windows systems, monitor user activity, and deliver arbitrary plugins or additional malware.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Creates mutex 'TEST'; deletes registry keys HKCU\Software\Console\IpDate and HKCU\Software\Console\IpDateInfo; stores C2 IP/port in HKCU\Software\Console\IpDateInfo = '|i:154.82.85.12|p:5689|'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At initial execution, the code ensures single instance, removes prior persistence, and stores C2 configuration in the registry, enabling future C2 communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry manipulation for C2 configuration and persistence is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not store C2 addresses in user registry keys or delete unrelated registry entries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use mutexes for single-instance enforcement.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Enumerates services for VM-related strings (e.g., 'VMWARE Tools', 'VirtualBox Guest'); terminates if found.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At startup, the code checks for virtualization artifacts and terminates if detected, evading analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: VM detection is a common anti-analysis technique in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely terminates based on VM presence.
key_indicators: Service name checks for VM artifacts

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Decodes shellcode with XOR 0x60; uses sleep obfuscation: modifies memory permissions, encodes/decodes shellcode, restores Sleep API, executes shellcode as callback for EnumSystemLocalesA.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During in-memory stage transition, the code obfuscates and executes shellcode to evade detection and load next-stage payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Memory permission manipulation and shellcode execution are hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not execute self-modifying shellcode in this manner.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Sets HKCU\Software\Classes\mscfile\Shell\Open\Command to loader path; creates scheduled task for loader; abuses eventvwr.msc/CompMgmtLauncher.exe for auto-elevation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During persistence setup, the code abuses registry and Windows auto-elevate mechanisms to ensure loader runs with high privileges at login.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry hijacking and auto-elevation abuse are common persistence and privilege escalation techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not hijack mscfile handlers or scheduled tasks for persistence.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Invoke-Command -Command {Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath C:\}; kills AV processes; modifies registry keys to disable AV autostart.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During AV evasion, the code disables Defender and other AV products, kills their processes, and disables autostart via registry.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling AV and killing security processes is a direct sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not disable security products.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Abuses ICMLuaUtil::ShellExec and fodhelper.exe with registry hijack (HKCU\Software\Classes\.pwn\Shell\Open\command, HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\CurVer) to launch malware with elevated privileges.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During privilege escalation, the code exploits Windows auto-elevate mechanisms to run itself as administrator without UAC prompt.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing COM and system tools for silent elevation is a known malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not hijack system handlers for elevation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Sends plaintext requests to C2 (e.g., GetRemoteShellcodeSize_{xor key}); receives XOR-encoded shellcode; injects into colorcpl.exe/cleanmgr.exe.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During C2 communication, the code requests, receives, decodes, and injects next-stage payloads into legitimate processes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Network-based payload delivery and process injection are core RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not fetch and inject shellcode from C2.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Sends '64' or '32' to C2; receives XOR-encoded payload downloader; reflectively loads DLL; requests final ValleyRAT payload; stores shellcode in registry value d33f351a4aeea5e608853d1a56661059 on HKCU\Console\1.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During payload delivery, the code downloads, decodes, and loads the ValleyRAT DLL, storing shellcode in the registry for stealthy execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Storing and executing shellcode from the registry is a stealthy malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not store executable code in registry values.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Supports commands: load plugin, write/execute file, download/execute from URL, send screenshots, clear event logs, update registry, enumerate processes, logoff/reboot/shutdown, create C2 session, prevent sleep, etc.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enables full remote control, data exfiltration, surveillance, and anti-forensics on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote control, surveillance, and anti-forensics are core RAT features.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not provide arbitrary remote control or clear event logs.

attack_chain.action: User executes malicious loader disguised as a financial document.
Loader obfuscates and executes in-memory shellcode to load next stage.
Beaconing module sets up persistence, disables AV, and escalates privileges.
Malware communicates with C2, downloads and injects next-stage payloads.
Payload downloader retrieves and loads ValleyRAT DLL, storing shellcode in registry.
ValleyRAT provides remote control, surveillance, and anti-forensics capabilities.

behavioral_signatures: In-memory shellcode execution with memory permission changes
Disabling/killing AV processes and modifying AV registry keys
Abuse of Windows auto-elevate mechanisms (eventvwr.msc, fodhelper.exe, ICMLuaUtil)
Process injection into legitimate Windows binaries (colorcpl.exe, cleanmgr.exe)
Registry-stored shellcode and reflective DLL loading
Remote command execution, screen capture, and event log clearing
file_indicators: Executables with Chinese financial document names (e.g., 工商年报大师.exe)
network_indicators: Plaintext C2 requests with XOR-encoded responses
Connections to http://www.baidu.com for connectivity check
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for suspicious registry modifications (especially under HKCU\Software\Console and HKCU\Software\Classes), in-memory shellcode execution with memory permission changes, process injection into system binaries, and AV process termination. Look for network traffic to known C2 IPs and plaintext requests with XOR-encoded responses. Detect creation of scheduled tasks or registry hijacks for persistence, and flag attempts to disable AV via PowerShell or registry. Alert on event log clearing, screen capture, and remote command execution behaviors.
